title: Hybrid Approach to Structural and Logical Analysis of DOCX Documents for Ensuring the Security of Electronic Document Management
content: This article addresses the need for structural and logical analysis of DOCX documents to ensure the security of electronic document management and automate compliance verification with established formatting requirements. Based on the analysis of scientific works, it has been established that most modern solutions in the field of document processing are oriented mainly towards PDF files, scanned images, or unstructured text data. In contrast, the DOCX format, in which the structure of a document is defined by styles, heading levels, sections, and embedded objects, remains insufficiently covered from the point of view of both structural analysis and information security. This necessitates the development of specialized approaches to the automated detection of the logical components of a document, the analysis of its internal structure, and the detection of potentially dangerous or hidden elements. The aim of the study is the development and experimental verification of a hybrid approach to the structural and logical analysis of DOCX documents for increasing the level of security of electronic document management. The proposed approach combines sequential parsing of the document content, style analysis, processing of formatting parameters, and the application of segmentation rules for identifying the title page, chapters, subsections, bibliography, tables, images, and appendices. The software implementation was carried out in Python using the python-docx library, which provides access to the internal XML structure of the file and allows preserving the semantic and visual parameters of the document. Additionally, the possibility of analyzing structural anomalies, hidden objects, and inconsistencies that may indicate potential security threats is provided. The result of the work is the construction of a standardized hierarchical JSON model suitable for further compliance control and security analysis of documents. Experimental testing of the created prototype on documents of different types confirmed its ability to correctly identify the main structural elements, restore the logical relationships between them, and form a unified internal representation of the document with high accuracy. The proposed approach makes it possible to detect structural anomalies and potentially dangerous elements of a document. The practical significance of the obtained results lies in the possibility of using the proposed approach not only for automating compliance control and standardization of documents, but also as a tool for increasing the level of information security in electronic document management systems.
